gaps.sentence: She ___ her grandmother every Sunday; it is a promise she never breaks.
gaps.hint: every Sunday marks repeated routine action
gaps.explanation: 'Every Sunday' signals a regularly repeated action, so the present simple is correct: visits.

gaps.sentence: The soup ___ delicious, but I think it needs a little more salt.
gaps.hint: taste describing a quality is stative
gaps.explanation: When 'taste' describes a quality of something, it is a state verb: tastes.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the match kicked off than it started pouring.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner had … than …' — past perfect with inversion.

gaps.sentence: By next April, we ___ here for ten years.
gaps.hint: duration leading up to a future point
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a future point takes the future perfect continuous: will have been living.

gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: Wait there and I ___ you some aspirin.
gaps.hint: a spontaneous offer at the moment
gaps.explanation: Offers made spontaneously at the moment of speaking use 'will': will get.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her laptop repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Has had it repaired twice this year' — present perfect of causative have.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ to traffic every year for repainting in May.
gaps.explanation: A recurring scheduled event takes the present simple.
